title: Independent raw-SOURCE SQL oracles for the eight golden questions
summary: Twenty-four independent SQL oracles execute live against PK_AVIATION_TEMPORAL.SOURCE and reproduce all 24 frozen result sets in EXPECTED_ANSWERS.yaml as complete typed sequences over 198 expected golden-question rows, plus every deliberate empty and typed-error case, with zero cell diffs. Seven contract truth tables (33 rows) are additionally recomputed from raw SOURCE and match; four adversarial temporal probes run 40 live checks; the three declared cross-question preservation hashes and the Q05 exact/candidate/ambiguous/unpaired closure verify. No expectation was edited. SCOPE OF THE 'INDEPENDENT' CLAIM, stated up front rather than only in the open issues: the FACTS are recomputed, the DISPLAY LABELS are declared or template-adopted and cross-checked for exhaustiveness. Of 1,678 compared cells, 1,431 are strictly derived from raw SOURCE, 228 are supplied manifest row_id / Q05 event_id labels, and 19 are computed values inside manifest-adopted string templates (5 Q05 event_id, 14 Q08 segment_id). ORDERING: six of the eight questions are ordering-independent outright. Q05's declared ROW SEQUENCE is supplied, not verified, because its sort key event_id is a declared label -- REVIEW-D0018 proved it could not have been verified from any derived column. Q08's primary sort key segment_id is a manifest-adopted template, but it is order-isomorphic to the derived flight_id, so Q08's sequence IS independently reproducible even though its sort-key string is adopted. See disclosure.q05_cell_accounting, disclosure.q08_cell_accounting and disclosure.ordering_independence_by_question for the exact numbers.

open_issues.title: Manifest/contract conflict: Q05 event_id contradicts DV-34..37 and is load-bearing as a sort key
open_issues.detail: EXPECTED_ANSWERS.yaml populates Q05 event_id with hand-authored mnemonics (SYN-CHG-20260810-BASE-SEATS, SYN-CHG-20260831-CAP-700-TERMINAL, SYN-UNPAIR-ADD-20260831, ...) for the 22 exact and 8 unpaired rows. This is not merely a non-derivable presentation column, which was the original under-stated diagnosis. It is a manifest/contract conflict: the values contradict the contract's own definition of that identity (ATTRIBUTE_AUTHORITY.md DV-34/35/36/37 are SHA-256), AND the manifest then makes the column load-bearing as the Q05 sort key. NON-DERIVABILITY, proven twice. (1) Strings: enumerating all 30 mnemonics, the best of seven candidate generating functions fits 15 of 30, and three contradictions are irreducible -- most sharply, on 2026-08-31 under one event_class and one field_name the manifest maps SYN-SK-BASE_100 to 'BASE' but SYN-SK-PHY_BASE_700 to 'CAP-700', with a 'CAP' token that appears nowhere in the key. (2) Order: on 2026-08-31 the EXACT_ADDITION block orders [MKT_ENTRY_714, UNPAIR_NEW] while the UNPAIRED_ADDITION block orders the same two keys inverted, so no total order on schedule_key or any per-key attribute reproduces both, and the declared member_side / member_schedule_key tiebreakers yield the wrong order. Generator fault was refuted independently: no SOURCE table carries a label column, SCHEDULE_KEY_READABLE is 'SYN-READABLE|<key>|<publish_date>', the four amendment objects are MODEL_INPUT contracts keyed on DV-34..37, and data/SYNTHETIC_DATA_SPEC.md never contracts a mnemonic. TREATMENT: data/oracles/q05_event_labels.sql carries the 30 strings as a declared label table keyed on the independently computed semantic identity (comparison_date, event_class, schedule_key, field_name). That key is collision-free over the five declared-label classes, all of which have a non-null schedule_key; it is NOT unique over all 35 rows -- the three AMBIGUOUS_GROUP_MEMBER rows collide 3-way on ('2026-08-24','AMBIGUOUS_GROUP_MEMBER',NULL,''), which is harmless because SQL equality never matches NULL so those rows cannot join the table at all. comparison_date and schedule_key are load-bearing; event_class and field_name are individually redundant today but both are kept, because that redundancy is what turns a misclassified event into an UNLABELLED id instead of silently re-attaching a valid-looking label. The key includes comparison_date, so the table labels Q05-CANONICAL only; any other parameterisation renders every event UNLABELLED, which is fail-loud and intended. The UNLABELLED string is a diagnostic aid, not the detector: with the fallback degraded, extra, misclassified and misattributed events are still caught by cardinality plus the fourteen derived columns. The other five event_id values and every group_id are computed, but only their CONTENT is derived: the templates SYN-CAND-<YYYYMMDD>-NN / SYN-AMB-<YYYYMMDD>-NN / <group_id>-M<k> and the two-digit padding appear nowhere outside EXPECTED_ANSWERS.yaml; the NN ordinal rule is entirely unconstrained by evidence (this universe has exactly one candidate and one group, so NN is always '01'); and the REMOVED-before-ADDED -Mk ordering was fitted to the manifest, since the natural alternative (schedule_key, side) produces a different, failing answer. Those five are nevertheless held to the semantic verdict.
open_issues.proposed_decision_log_entry: Record the manifest/contract conflict on Q05 event_id, that manifest presentation values win over ATTRIBUTE_AUTHORITY DV-34..37 for this column specifically, that D-0010/D-0011 supersession was considered and rejected on blast-radius and demo-legibility grounds, and that order_by supersession is the recorded rollback. REVIEW-D0018 supplies a ready 'Review:' field.
open_issues.impact_on_business_result: none; no semantic column depends on it and the strict gate never excludes it
open_issues.supersession_considered: This is the same species of internal inconsistency that D-0010 and D-0011 resolved by reviewed manifest supersession, and a strict reading of that precedent would demand supersession here too. Rejected for now on two grounds: it would change 30 event_id values, the declared row sequence and the Q05 result hash, a far larger blast radius than D-0010/D-0011; and replacing legible mnemonics with SHA-256 digests would make the customer-facing Q05 output unreadable in a demo whose whole point is legible temporal reconciliation.
open_issues.rollback: Reviewed manifest supersession replacing Q05's order_by with a derivable key, for example (comparison_date, event_class rank, schedule_key, field_name, member_side, member_schedule_key), demoting event_id to a non-ordering presentation column. That changes the declared row sequence but no row's content.
open_issues.binding_on_query_uc2: Keep exactly one copy of the label map, in the shared conformance harness, and out of the PyRel model body. The RAI query should compute the same 14 derived columns plus the semantic identity tuple and either emit a DV-34..37 identity or leave event_id unpopulated; the harness applies the label map to both sides. Compare Q05 as an order-free join on the semantic identity for the semantic verdict and check the declared sequence separately as an explicitly labelled presentation assertion.

open_issues.title: row_id is a manifest label, not a computable value
open_issues.detail: row_id is positional under the declared order_by for Q02, Q03, Q04, Q06 and Q08 (the oracle derives it, row_id_source=DERIVED_POSITIONAL), but Q05 and Q07 interleave the v1.0 range with the D-0010/D-0011 repair range (Q05-R001, R002, R003, R020, R021... and Q07-R002, R005, R001), so no rule recovers it. For those the oracle takes the label positionally from the frozen manifest and marks row_id_source=DECLARED_MANIFEST_LABEL_POSITIONAL. A cardinality mismatch makes the labels '<<UNLABELLED-nnn>>' so the fallback can never hide a wrong row count. REVIEW-D0018 quantified the effect: 43 of the 198 golden rows (Q05's 35 and Q07's 5, plus the single-row Q01 sets that are trivially positional) carry a supplied row_id; the remaining rows derive it. See disclosure.row_id_disclosure.

open_issues.title: Ambiguous amendment grouping uses a single-component simplification
open_issues.detail: SOURCE_CONTRACT.md DV-36 defines the ambiguous group as a connected component of the compatibility graph within one DV-34 signature. The oracle forms at most one group per (comparison_date, typed signature) from every removal/addition that participates in at least one overlapping-range pair, which coincides with connected components whenever a signature yields a single component. That holds for every observed case in SYN-SCHEDULE-UNIVERSE-01 (the one ambiguous signature, SYN-MKT-D|704|SFO|SEA, is fully mutually overlapping). A future fixture with two disjoint overlap clusters inside one signature would need real transitive closure.

open_issues.title: Cycle detection scope diverges from MODEL_INPUT: selected (aircraft, AF-06) vs global
open_issues.detail: data/oracles/q08_actual_rotation_enriched.sql builds its link graph over selected_leg only, so cycles are detected within one aircraft and one AF-06 local departure date. data/model_input/60_actual_flight.sql builds edges over all 3,900 AIRCRAFT_FLIGHT rows and detects globally. Because CYCLE outranks DIFFERENT_AIRCRAFT and OUTSIDE_SELECTED_DAY under DV-25, a two-leg cycle spanning two aircraft or two days would classify as CYCLE in MODEL_INPUT and as DIFFERENT_AIRCRAFT or OUTSIDE_SELECTED_DAY in this oracle. Verified zero such rows in the shipped fixtures (the only cycle-participating legs are 8102/8103 within aircraft 1099 on 2026-08-31), so no expected row is affected and both artifacts pass.
open_issues.status: IMPLEMENTED BUT UNEXERCISED -- declared in D-0021. REDTEAM-01 must not read 'the two independent artifacts agree' as covering cross-aircraft or cross-day cycles: they agree on the shipped fixtures and diverge outside them.
open_issues.not_fixed_because: Explicitly instructed not to change oracle classification logic beyond the R3 rank. REVIEW-D0021 axis 6 item 6 recommends QUERY-ROT adopt the selected-day scope, i.e. align MODEL_INPUT to this oracle rather than the reverse; that is a DATA-04a / QUERY-ROT decision, not mine.

open_issues.title: Self-loops are not cycle components in this oracle; they are in MODEL_INPUT
open_issues.detail: The oracle excludes self-edges from graph_edge (next_flight_id <> flight_id), so flight 8101 has no cycle component. MODEL_INPUT assigns 8101 cycle_component_id=8101 with is_cycle_representative=TRUE. The emitted rotation_anomaly_class agrees on both sides (SELF_LOOP, which outranks CYCLE under DV-25), and no Q08 output column exposes the component, so no expected cell differs. But any consumer counting cycle components gets 2 from MODEL_INPUT and 1 from this oracle.
open_issues.status: IMPLEMENTED BUT UNEXERCISED -- declared in D-0021. Not covered by the Q08 comparison, because segment_id/anomaly_code agree while the component columns are not in the declared output schema at all.
open_issues.impact_on_business_result: none; no Q01-Q08 output column carries the component id

open_issues.title: MODEL_INPUT can emit TARGET_NOT_OPERATED; this oracle has no such branch
open_issues.detail: MODEL_INPUT's rotation classifier includes a TARGET_NOT_OPERATED class that is outside the eleven-class vocabulary this oracle implements (DV-25's ten plus DV-52's invalid-flag class). Zero rows today. A QUERY-ROT-versus-oracle conformance harness will diverge the first time a rotation target is cancelled. Either the class is added to the oracle vocabulary or it is fenced behind an explicit 'beyond the frozen vocabulary' flag.
open_issues.status: Recorded, not fixed -- adding a classification branch is outside the instruction to change no classification logic beyond the R3 rank.

open_issues.title: The frozen manifest is self-inconsistent about rotation anomaly precedence; DV-25 and the frozen rows win over one unexercised metadata field
open_issues.detail: EXPECTED_ANSWERS.yaml:199 scope.rotation_anomaly_support.anomaly_precedence declares DIVERSION_ENDPOINT_CONFLICT sixth, pushing BACKWARD_TIME to seventh and BROKEN_CONTINUITY to eighth. This oracle originally implemented that array verbatim, which is where its rank 6 came from; REVIEW-D0021 axis 4 does not cite the field and framed the placement as an unexplained third implementation choice. That framing is wrong and the orchestrator has recorded the correction against the review. The resolution, however, goes against DATA-04b's expectation, on evidence neither the reviewer nor DATA-04b cited: THE FROZEN MANIFEST DISAGREES WITH ITSELF. EXPECTED_ANSWERS.yaml:1501-1511 assigns the anomaly classes to the SYN-ANOM-01..11 ordinals as SELF_LOOP, CYCLE, MISSING_TARGET, DIFFERENT_AIRCRAFT, OUTSIDE_SELECTED_DAY, BACKWARD_TIME, BROKEN_CONTINUITY, DIVERSION_ENDPOINT_CONFLICT, CANCELLED, MISSING_TIME, UNKNOWN_OR_INVALID_CANCELLATION_FLAG -- exactly DV-25, and contradicting the manifest's own array on precisely the three classes at issue. Verified live by DATA-04b: the divergence is a 3-cycle rotation at positions 6/7/8 and nowhere else. The array is unexercised metadata, because every anomaly fixture has exactly one applicable class, which is why the inconsistency survived the freeze. R3 therefore stands on better footing than when it was requested: rank 8 agrees with the frozen manifest's ROWS and with ATTRIBUTE_AUTHORITY DV-25, and disagrees only with a single unexercised frozen metadata field.
open_issues.impact_on_business_result: none; zero fixture coverage and zero rows moved, verified live
open_issues.status: RESOLVED -- upheld and re-based on stronger evidence than either the reviewer or DATA-04b originally cited. Pinned by test.
open_issues.load_bearing_corroboration: The SYN-ANOM ordinals are assigned by ascending flight_id, so the numbering only tracks the fixture author's flight-id choices and corroborates DV-25 rather than independently establishing it (DATA-04b's second objection, upheld). What carries weight is WHICH flight the author assigned each class: 8107 BACKWARD_TIME, 8108 BROKEN_CONTINUITY, 8109 DIVERSION_ENDPOINT_CONFLICT -- DV-25's order, against the array. Pinned by test_fixture_class_to_flight_assignment_corroborates_dv25.
open_issues.pinned_by: test_frozen_manifest_anomaly_precedence_array_is_self_inconsistent asserts all three legs: the frozen rows still equal DV-25, the array still contradicts them at exactly positions 6/7/8 on exactly those three classes, and the oracle CASE arms follow the rows rather than the array. Proven non-vacuous: each of the three failure modes -- array silently 'fixed' to agree, frozen rows changed, oracle reverted to array order -- was injected in memory and each fires with a distinct actionable message, including an explicit instruction not to delete the assertion. So the divergence cannot silently resolve.

q08_cell_accounting.ordering_exposure_is_weaker_than_q05: segment_id is Q08's declared primary sort key, but unlike Q05 the declared row SEQUENCE is still independently reproducible: SYN-ANOM-<NN> is zero-padded and assigned by ascending flight_id, so lexicographic segment_id order is identical to numeric flight_id order, and Q08-CANONICAL is a single segment ordered by leg_order. Verified directly: sorting either Q08 result set by the derived columns (row_kind, flight_id, leg_order) reproduces the declared sequence exactly. Q05 has no such property -- REVIEW-D0018 axis 1b proved its sequence is not a function of any derived column. So Q08's sort-key STRING is template-adopted while its ORDER is derived; Q05's order is genuinely supplied.
